✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Cube Calculations:
• (a) Total cubes: Volume = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 unit cubes.
• (b) Cubes painted on 3 faces: Only the 8 corner cubes have three exposed faces painted red.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Total: 27 unit cubes 1.5 M
Corner cubes: 8 cubes 1.5 M
Q11 A triangular prism (like a chocolate Toblerone box) has two triangular ends and three rectangular sides. How many faces, edges, and vertices does it have in total? Textbook Exercise • Triangular Prism Net 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Triangular Prism Properties:
• Faces: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles = 5 faces.
• Edges: 3 on top triangle + 3 on bottom triangle + 3 connecting vertical edges = 9 edges.
• Vertices: 3 corners on each triangle = 6 vertices.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
5 faces 1 M
9 edges 1 M
6 vertices 1 M
Q12 Navin made a bridge model using matchboxes. He placed 6 matchboxes side by side to make the span, and supported them on two piles of 3 matchboxes each. How many matchboxes did he use in all? Textbook Exercise • Matchbox Model 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Matchbox Addition:
• Bridge span: 6 matchboxes.
• Supports: 2 piles of 3 matchboxes = 2 × 3 = 6 matchboxes.
• Total matchboxes: 6 + 6 = 12 matchboxes.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Span and support breakdown 1 M
Total: 12 matchboxes 1 M
Q13 What is 'Isometric Dot Paper', and why is it preferred for drawing 3D cubes and cuboids over ordinary square grid paper? Textbook Exercise • Isometric Dot Paper Drawing 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Isometric Dot Paper:
• Isometric dot paper has dots arranged in equilateral triangular grids.
• It allows artists to draw receding parallel lines at 30° angles to show true 3D depth and proportion without distortion, making edges of equal length look natural in 3D.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Description of triangular dot grid 1 M
30° perspective / true depth advantage 1 M
Q14 A pyramid with a square base has 4 triangular faces meeting at a top point. (a) Describe its flat net. (b) How many edges does a square pyramid have? Textbook Exercise • Square Pyramid Net 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Square Pyramid:
• (a) Net description: A central square with 4 identical triangles attached to each of its four edges (resembling a 4-pointed star).
• (b) Edges: 4 edges on the square base + 4 slanting edges meeting at the top vertex = 8 edges.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Star-like net described 1 M
8 edges stated 1 M
Q15 A cylindrical glass tumbler with water is viewed from: (a) Directly from the top (b) From the side at eye level. Describe the shape seen in each view. Textbook Exercise • Views of a Glass Tumbler 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Tumbler Views:
• (a) Top View: You see concentric circles (the circular rim and base).
• (b) Side View: You see a rectangle (or trapezoid if the glass is tapered).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Top: Circles 1 M
Side: Rectangle / Trapezoid 1 M
Q16 You have a sheet of graph paper. You want to make a cube with side 4 cm. What should be the area of each square on the net, and what is the total paper area needed? Textbook Exercise • Cube Puzzle from Paper 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Cube Paper Area:
• Area of one square face = 4 cm × 4 cm = 16 sq cm.
• A cube has 6 faces.
• Total paper area needed: 6 × 16 sq cm = 96 sq cm.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
One face area: 16 sq cm 1 M
Total area: 96 sq cm 1 M
Q17 A 3 × 3 × 3 solid block of 27 cubes is placed on a table. How many unit cubes are completely hidden inside and cannot be seen from any angle from the outside? Textbook Exercise • Hidden Cubes in a Solid Block 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Internal Cube:
• Only the 1 central core cube (at row 2, column 2, layer 2) has no exposed faces to the outside.
• Therefore, exactly 1 cube is completely hidden.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Central core identified 1 M
1 hidden cube stated 1 M
Q18 How many faces, edges, and vertices does a perfect sphere (like a football) have? Textbook Exercise • Sphere Properties 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Sphere Properties:
• Faces: 1 continuous curved surface (no flat faces).
• Edges: 0 edges (no straight or sharp boundaries).
• Vertices: 0 vertices (no corners).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
1 curved surface 1 M
0 edges and 0 vertices 1 M
Q19 Looking at a staircase of 4 steps: (a) What does the side view look like? (b) What does the top view look like? Textbook Exercise • Staircase View Problem 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Staircase Views:
• (a) Side View: A stepped zigzag outline (staircase profile showing 4 risers and 4 treads).
• (b) Top View: A single large rectangle divided into 4 equal parallel horizontal strips (the steps).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Side: Stepped zigzag profile 1 M
Top: 4 parallel rectangular strips 1 M
Q20 A T-shaped cube net has 4 squares in a vertical column and 2 squares attached to the left and right of the second square from top. Explain how folding this net makes a cube. Textbook Exercise • T-Net of a Cube 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Folding Process:
1. The second square acts as the base.
2. The left and right squares fold upwards at 90° to form the left and right walls.
3. The top square folds down to form the front wall.
4. The two bottom squares fold up: the third square forms the back wall and the fourth square folds over the top to form the lid. This perfectly closes all 6 faces of the cube.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Base identification 1 M
Folding steps for 4 sides and lid 2 M
Q21 State three key differences between a 2-Dimensional (2D) shape and a 3-Dimensional (3D) shape. Textbook Exercise • Difference between 2D and 3D Shapes 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Differences:
1. Dimensions: 2D shapes have only 2 dimensions (length and width). 3D shapes have 3 dimensions (length, width, and height/depth).
2. Flatness: 2D shapes are completely flat and lie entirely within a plane. 3D shapes occupy physical space in the real world.
3. Measurement: 2D shapes are measured by Area (sq units). 3D shapes are measured by Volume (cubic units).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
3 clear differences stated (1 M each) 3 M
Q22 Euler's formula for any simple polyhedron is: Faces (F) + Vertices (V) - Edges (E) = 2. Verify this formula for: (a) A Cube (b) A Triangular Prism. Textbook Exercise • Euler's Formula for Polyhedra 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Euler's Formula Verification (F + V - E = 2):
• (a) Cube: F = 6, V = 8, E = 12.
Calculation: 6 + 8 - 12 = 14 - 12 = 2 (Verified!).
• (b) Triangular Prism: F = 5, V = 6, E = 9.
Calculation: 5 + 6 - 9 = 11 - 9 = 2 (Verified!).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Formula stated 1 M
Cube verification (6+8-12=2) 1 M
Prism verification (5+6-9=2) 1 M
Q23 A shoe box is 30 cm long, 18 cm wide, and 12 cm high. How many square centimetres of wrapping paper are needed to cover the entire box completely? Textbook Exercise • Shoe Box Dimensions 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Total Surface Area of Cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl):
• lb = 30 × 18 = 540 sq cm.
• bh = 18 × 12 = 216 sq cm.
• hl = 12 × 30 = 360 sq cm.
• Sum = 540 + 216 + 360 = 1,116 sq cm.
• Total Surface Area = 2 × 1,116 = 2,232 sq cm.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Surface area formula stated 1 M
Face products calculated 1 M
Final answer: 2,232 sq cm 1 M
Q24 (a) What is the shape of the flat base of a cone? (b) How many flat faces does a cylinder have, and what shape are they? Textbook Exercise • Cone vs Cylinder Base 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Base Shapes:
• (a) Cone base: A flat Circle.
• (b) Cylinder flat faces: Exactly 2 flat circular faces (one top, one bottom).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Cone: Circle 1 M
Cylinder: 2 circular faces 1 M

Chapter 10: Tenths and Hundredths

दसवाँ और सौवाँ भाग (दशमलव, मिलीमीटर-सेंटीमीटर एवं मुद्रा गणना)

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (24 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Mathematical Ideas & Key Properties
  • Understanding Decimals: Tenths (1/10 = 0.1) and Hundredths (1/100 = 0.01).
  • Length measurement: 1 cm = 10 mm ⇒ 1 mm = 0.1 cm.
  • Currency notation: 1 Rupee = 100 paise ⇒ 1 paisa = ₹0.01; 75 paise = ₹0.75.
  • Temperature reading and comparing decimal values across different Indian cities.
  • (a) 4 cm 8 mm: Since $1\text{ mm} = 0.1\text{ cm}$, $8\text{ mm} = 0.8\text{ cm}$. Total = $4 + 0.8 = \mathbf{4.8\text{ cm}}$.
  • (b) 75 paise: Since $100\text{ paise} = ₹1$, $75\text{ paise} = \frac{75}{100} = \mathbf{₹0.75}$.
  • (c) 3 m 45 cm: Since $100\text{ cm} = 1\text{ m}$, $45\text{ cm} = 0.45\text{ m}$. Total = $3 + 0.45 = \mathbf{3.45\text{ m}}$.
  • (d) 5 mm: $\frac{5}{10} = \mathbf{0.5\text{ cm}}$.

Q1 Look at a ruler: (a) How many millimetres are there in 1 centimetre? (b) What fraction of a centimetre is 1 mm? (c) A small pencil measures 3 cm and 6 mm. Write its length in centimetres using decimals. Textbook Exercise • Pencil Measurement in Millimetres 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Metric Conversions:
• (a) Millimetres in 1 cm: 10 millimetres (10 mm).
• (b) Fraction: 1 mm = 1/10 of a cm.
• (c) Decimal notation: 3 cm + 6/10 cm = 3.6 cm.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Part (a): 10 mm 1 M
Part (b): 1/10 cm 1 M
Part (c): 3.6 cm 1 M

Calculations:

CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Part (a): 9 mm 1.5 M
Part (b): About 33-34 frogs 1.5 M

Q9 Put >, < or = between the decimal numbers:
(a) 0.5 and 0.05
(b) 3.45 and 3.54
(c) 1.20 and 1.2
(d) 0.89 and 0.9 Textbook Exercise • Comparing Decimals 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Decimal Comparisons:
• (a) 0.5 & 0.05: 5 tenths > 0 tenths. 0.5 > 0.05.
• (b) 3.45 & 3.54: 4 tenths < 5 tenths. 3.45 < 3.54.
• (c) 1.20 & 1.2: Trailing zeros do not change value. 1.20 = 1.2.
• (d) 0.89 & 0.9: 0.89 < 0.90 (8 tenths < 9 tenths). 0.89 < 0.9.

Chapter 11: Area and its Boundary

क्षेत्रफल और घेरा (परिमाप, डाक टिकट क्षेत्रफल एवं राजा का सोने का तार)

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (24 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Mathematical Ideas & Key Properties
  • Perimeter = Total length of the boundary: P = 2 × (L + B) for rectangles, P = 4 × S for squares.
  • Area = Measure of region enclosed: A = L × B for rectangles, A = S × S for squares.
  • Shapes with the SAME perimeter can enclose DIFFERENT areas.
  • A square encloses the maximum area for any given rectangular perimeter.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (24 Solved Questions)
Q1 Arbaaz planned to divide his land equally among his three children—Nasreen, Shahid, and Zaid. He wanted to give each child 30 square metres of land. Nasreen's land is 5 m long and 6 m wide. Shahid's land is 3 m wide and 10 m long. Zaid's land is 2 m wide and 15 m long.
(a) Find the area of each child's land.
(b) Who got the land with the longest boundary (perimeter)? Textbook Exercise • Land Division among Three Children 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Perimeter & Area Calculations:
• (a) Areas:
- Nasreen: 5 m × 6 m = 30 sq m.
- Shahid: 3 m × 10 m = 30 sq m.
- Zaid: 2 m × 15 m = 30 sq m.
• (b) Boundaries (Perimeter = 2 × (l + b)):
- Nasreen: 2 × (5 + 6) = 2 × 11 = 22 metres.
- Shahid: 2 × (3 + 10) = 2 × 13 = 26 metres.
- Zaid: 2 × (2 + 15) = 2 × 17 = 34 metres.
• Zaid got the land with the longest boundary (34 metres).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
All three areas equal 30 sq m 1.5 M
Perimeter calculations: 22, 26, 34 m 1.5 M
Conclusion: Zaid has longest boundary 1 M
Q2 How can you cut a small 14 cm × 9 cm postcard in a continuous spiral strip so that it opens into a huge belt large enough for a person to pass through? Textbook Exercise • Postcard Loop (Paper Cutting Trick) 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Postcard Belt Cutting Technique:
1. Fold the postcard in half along its length.
2. Cut narrow parallel slits starting alternately from the folded edge and from the open edge, leaving a small 2 mm margin at each turn so the strip is not severed completely.
3. Cut open the folds of the inner loops (leaving the two end loops intact).
4. Pull the paper gently: the thin cuts unfold into a huge continuous zigzag paper belt with a perimeter exceeding 2 to 3 metres, allowing a child or adult to step right through!
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Alternating slit cutting procedure explained 2 M
Continuous loop expansion explained 1 M
Q3 A square field has a side of 40 metres. (a) What is the total length of wire needed to put a fence of 4 rounds around the field? (b) If fencing costs ₹15 per metre, what is the cost of fencing? (c) If ploughing the field costs ₹2 per square metre, what is the cost of ploughing? Textbook Exercise • Cost of Fencing vs Tiling 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Step-by-step Solution:
• (a) Wire length: Perimeter of 1 round = 4 × 40 m = 160 m. For 4 rounds = 4 × 160 = 640 metres.
• (b) Cost of fencing: 640 m × ₹15 = ₹9,600.
• (c) Cost of ploughing: Area = 40 m × 40 m = 1,600 sq m. Cost = 1,600 × ₹2 = ₹3,200.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Wire length: 640 m 1.5 M
Fencing cost: ₹9,600 1 M
Ploughing cost: ₹3,200 1.5 M

Perimeter of Saree:
• Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Width) = 2 × (5.5 + 1.2) = 2 × 6.7 = 13.4 metres.

Formula 2(l + w) 1 M
Answer: 13.4 metres 1 M
Q5 Two rectangular vegetable plots both have a perimeter of 36 metres: Plot A is 10 m long and 8 m wide. Plot B is 12 m long and 6 m wide. (a) Verify that both plots have the same perimeter. (b) Find the area of Plot A and Plot B. (c) Which plot gives more area to grow vegetables? Textbook Exercise • Comparing Rectangles with Equal Perimeter 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Comparison:
• (a) Perimeters:
- Plot A: 2 × (10 + 8) = 2 × 18 = 36 m.
- Plot B: 2 × (12 + 6) = 2 × 18 = 36 m. (Verified!).
• (b) Areas:
- Area of Plot A = 10 × 8 = 80 sq m.
- Area of Plot B = 12 × 6 = 72 sq m.
• (c) Conclusion: Plot A gives 80 - 72 = 8 sq m more area (shapes closer to a square maximize area!).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Verification of perimeters 1 M
Areas: 80 sq m and 72 sq m 2 M
Plot A gives more area 1 M

Q7 A loop of string of length 20 cm is placed on a table: (a) If it forms a square, what is its area? (b) If it forms a rectangle of width 4 cm, what is its area? (c) Which shape has greater area? Textbook Exercise • Thread Loop Shape Shifting 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
String Loop (Perimeter = 20 cm):
• (a) Square: Side = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm. Area = 5 × 5 = 25 sq cm.
• (b) Rectangle: Width = 4 cm. Length = (20 ÷ 2) - 4 = 10 - 4 = 6 cm. Area = 6 × 4 = 24 sq cm.
• (c) Conclusion: The Square has greater area by 1 sq cm.

Square area: 25 sq cm 1 M
Rectangle area: 24 sq cm 1 M

Q14 A wire bent into the shape of a rectangle of 18 cm by 12 cm is straightened and then rebent into a square. (a) What is the length of the wire? (b) What will be the side of the square? (c) Which shape encloses more area? Textbook Exercise • Wire Shape Transition 4 Marks

Q16 A rectangle has length 6 cm and width 4 cm. If both its length and width are tripled: (a) What happens to its perimeter? (b) What happens to its area? Textbook Exercise • Tripling the Dimensions of a Rectangle 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Tripling Scaling:
• Original: Perimeter = 2(6+4) = 20 cm; Area = 6×4 = 24 sq cm.
• New dimensions: Length = 18 cm, Width = 12 cm.
• (a) New Perimeter: 2(18+12) = 60 cm (3 times larger).
• (b) New Area: 18 × 12 = 216 sq cm (9 times larger, since 3² = 9).

Q17 Two identical square desks of side 80 cm are pushed together side-by-side to form one long rectangular conference table. (a) What are the dimensions of the new table? (b) What is its perimeter? (c) Did the perimeter double? Explain. Textbook Exercise • Perimeter of Combined Tables 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Combined Desks:
• (a) Dimensions: Length = 80 + 80 = 160 cm; Width = 80 cm.
• (b) Perimeter: 2 × (160 + 80) = 2 × 240 = 480 cm.
• (c) Perimeter double test: Individual desk perimeter = 4 × 80 = 320 cm. Double would be 640 cm. The perimeter did NOT double because two 80 cm edges are joined internally and no longer form part of the boundary.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Dimensions: 160 cm × 80 cm 1 M
Perimeter: 480 cm 1.5 M

Q24 Why is perimeter measured in linear units (like cm or metres) while area is measured in square units (like sq cm or sq metres)? Explain clearly. Textbook Exercise • Unit of Area vs Unit of Perimeter 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Units Conceptual Distinction:
• Perimeter: Measures the total 1-dimensional length of the surrounding boundary line. It is a distance, so it is measured in linear units (cm, m).
• Area: Measures the 2-dimensional surface region enclosed inside the boundary. It counts how many unit squares (1 cm × 1 cm or 1 m × 1 m) fit inside, so it is measured in square units (sq cm, sq m).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
1D boundary length concept for perimeter 1 M
2D square count concept for area 1 M

- Cycle (28): 5 complete boxes of five + 3 lines (5 × 5 + 3 = 28).
- Bus (15): 3 complete boxes of five (5 × 3 = 15).
• (b) Total vehicles: 28 + 12 + 18 + 15 + 24 + 6 = 103 vehicles.
• (c) Most observed vehicle: Cycle (28).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Tally mark representation 1.5 M

Q3 Rabbits were brought to an island. The table shows their numbers each year:
• Year 0: 10 rabbits

• Year 2: 32 rabbits
• Year 3: 58 rabbits
• Year 4: 108 rabbits
(a) Is the rabbit population growing by adding a fixed number or by multiplying? (b) Predict the approximate number of rabbits in Year 5. Textbook Exercise • Rabbit Population Growth Table 3 Marks

• (b) Year 5 prediction: Approximately double of 108 minus 10 ≈ 216 - 10 = around 200 to 210 rabbits.

Multiplicative / doubling trend identified 1.5 M

Q4 A plant's height was measured every 4 days:

• (b) Total growth: 11.1 - 0 = 11.1 cm.

Interval analysis 1 M

Q15 Explain how NCERT Class 5 tally marks are drawn using the 5-line box method. Textbook Exercise • Tally Box Notation 3 Marks

• 3 = 3 sides of a square (U)
• 4 = A complete square (4 sides: 🗆)
• 5 = A square with a diagonal slash crossing it (🗎).
This creates easy-to-read bundles of 5.

Q1 Maniratnam is the cashier of King Jayan. His job is to calculate the salary of all the workers: The cook gets ₹65 per day, the minister gets ₹195 per day, and the king's horse-keeper gets ₹86 per day. Calculate:
(a) The cook's salary for the month of January (31 days).
(b) The horse-keeper's salary for 1 full year (365 days).
(c) The minister's salary for 1 full year (365 days). Textbook Exercise • Maniratnam the Cashier (Daily Wage Multiplications) 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Multiplication Calculations:
• (a) Cook's salary for January: 31 × ₹65 = 31 × (60 + 5) = 1,860 + 155 = ₹2,015.
• (b) Horse-keeper's annual salary: 365 × ₹86 = 365 × (80 + 6) = 29,200 + 2,190 = ₹31,390.
• (c) Minister's annual salary: 365 × ₹195 = 365 × (200 - 5) = 73,000 - 1,825 = ₹71,175.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Cook: ₹2,015 1 M
Horse-keeper: ₹31,390 1.5 M
Minister: ₹71,175 1.5 M
Q2 Multiply 47 × 19 using Bela's method (distributive method by splitting 19 into 9 and 10). Show each partial product. Textbook Exercise • Bela's Method of Multiplication 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Bela's Distributive Method:
Split 19 = 10 + 9:
• Step 1: Multiply 47 by 9 = 47 × 9 = 423.
• Step 2: Multiply 47 by 10 = 47 × 10 = 470.
• Step 3: Add partial products = 423 + 470 = 893.
Therefore, 47 × 19 = 893.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
47 × 9 = 423 1 M
47 × 10 = 470 1 M
Sum: 893 1 M
Q3 Shantaram is a special cook who is called only on party days. Last year he was called for only 28 days. For each day he is paid ₹165. (a) How much money did he earn in all? (b) If he was paid for all 365 days of the year, how much would he have earned? Textbook Exercise • Shantaram the Cook's Holiday Deduction 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Calculations:
• (a) Actual earnings: 28 × ₹165 = 28 × (100 + 60 + 5) = 2,800 + 1,680 + 140 = ₹4,620.
• (b) Full year earnings: 365 × ₹165 = 365 × (100 + 60 + 5) = 36,500 + 21,900 + 1,825 = ₹60,225.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
28 days earnings: ₹4,620 1.5 M
Full year earnings: ₹60,225 1.5 M

Q10 A sweet maker has 250 laddoos. He packs them into boxes of 12 laddoos each. (a) How many full boxes can he make? (b) How many laddoos will be left over? (c) How many more laddoos are needed to make another full box? Textbook Exercise • Division with Remainder (Laddoo Packing) 3 Marks

Q12 Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. Divide 678 by 14 and verify your result using this formula. Textbook Exercise • Verifying Division (Dividend Formula) 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Division and Verification:
1. Division: 678 ÷ 14 = 48 with remainder 6 (since 14 × 40 = 560; 118 ÷ 14 = 8 with remainder 6: 14 × 8 = 112, 118 - 112 = 6).
2. Verification:
- Divisor × Quotient = 14 × 48 = 672.
- Adding remainder: 672 + 6 = 678 (Dividend). (Verified!).

Formula verification shown 1.5 M

Q18 Explain how 96 ÷ 16 can be solved using repeated subtraction. How many times can 16 be subtracted from 96? Textbook Exercise • Repeated Subtraction Division 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Repeated Subtraction:
• 96 - 16 = 80 (1st)
• 80 - 16 = 64 (2nd)
• 64 - 16 = 48 (3rd)
• 48 - 16 = 32 (4th)
• 32 - 16 = 16 (5th)
• 16 - 16 = 0 (6th)
16 was subtracted exactly 6 times. Therefore, 96 ÷ 16 = 6.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Subtraction steps shown 1 M
Quotient = 6 1 M

Chapter 14: How Big? How Heavy?

कितना बड़ा? कितना भारी? (आयतन, घन सेमी, जल विस्थापन एवं भार तुलना)

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (24 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Mathematical Ideas & Key Properties
  • Volume is the 3D space occupied by an object: Volume of Cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height.
  • Standard unit of volume: Cubic centimetre (cu cm or cm³).
  • Water displacement method: Volume of an irregular solid = Volume of water displaced.
  • Packing volume: Number of small unit cubes that can fit into a larger carton box.
  • Given: Volume displaced by 6 marbles = 12 ml.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (24 Solved Questions)
Q1 A measuring glass filled with water to 50 mL mark rises to 68 mL when 9 equal glass marbles are dropped inside.
(a) How much water was displaced by all 9 marbles?
(b) What is the volume of 1 marble in mL?
(c) What is the volume in cubic centimetres (cm³) if 1 mL = 1 cm³? Textbook Exercise • Measuring Volume with Marbles 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Volume by Water Displacement:
• (a) Displaced water: 68 mL - 50 mL = 18 mL.
• (b) Volume of 1 marble: 18 mL ÷ 9 marbles = 2 mL.
• (c) In cubic centimetres: 2 mL = 2 cm³.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Part (a): 18 mL 1 M
Part (b): 2 mL 1 M
Part (c): 2 cm³ 1 M
Q2 (a) What is the formula for the volume of a cube? (b) Find the volume of a wooden cube of side 5 cm. (c) How many 1 cm unit cubes can fit inside it? Textbook Exercise • Volume of a Cube 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Volume of Cube:
• (a) Formula: Volume = Side × Side × Side = Side³.
• (b) Volume: 5 cm × 5 cm × 5 cm = 125 cm³.
• (c) Number of 1 cm unit cubes: 125 ÷ 1 = 125 cubes.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Formula: Side³ 1 M
Volume: 125 cm³ 1 M
125 unit cubes fit 1 M
Q3 A matchbox measures 5 cm in length, 3 cm in width, and 1 cm in height. (a) What is the volume of one matchbox? (b) What is the volume of a packet containing 12 such matchboxes? Textbook Exercise • Volume of a Cuboid 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Volume Calculations (Volume = l × w × h):
• (a) One matchbox: 5 cm × 3 cm × 1 cm = 15 cm³.
• (b) Packet of 12 matchboxes: 12 × 15 cm³ = 180 cm³.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
One matchbox: 15 cm³ 1.5 M
Packet: 180 cm³ 1.5 M
Q4 A carton box is 20 cm long, 10 cm wide, and 8 cm high. How many soap cakes of size 5 cm × 5 cm × 4 cm can be packed inside the carton box? Textbook Exercise • Packing Cubes into a Carton 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Packing Capacity:
• Method 1 (Dimensions fitting):
- Along 20 cm length: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 soaps.
- Along 10 cm width: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 soaps.
- Along 8 cm height: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 soaps.
- Total soaps = 4 × 2 × 2 = 16 soaps.
• Method 2 (Volume): Volume of carton = 20 × 10 × 8 = 1,600 cm³. Volume of 1 soap = 5 × 5 × 4 = 100 cm³. Number of soaps = 1,600 ÷ 100 = 16 soaps.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Dimension fitting / Volume method 1.5 M
Answer: 16 soaps 1.5 M

Total matchboxes: 42 1.5 M
Total volume: 630 cm³ 1.5 M

1,000 coins 1 M
Value: ₹5,000 1 M

Q8 Fill in the blanks: (a) 1 litre = _____ mL. (b) 1 mL = _____ cm³. (c) 1 litre = _____ cm³. Textbook Exercise • Litres and Millilitres to Cubic Centimetres 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Volume Equivalences:
• (a) 1 litre = 1,000 mL.
• (b) 1 mL = 1 cm³.
• (c) 1 litre = 1,000 mL = 1,000 cm³.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
1,000 mL 1 M
1 cm³ 1 M
1,000 cm³ 1 M
Q9 A rectangular overhead water tank is 2 metres long, 1.5 metres wide, and 1 metre high. (a) What is its volume in cubic metres? (b) How many litres of water can it hold if 1 cubic metre (m³) = 1,000 litres? Textbook Exercise • Water Tank Capacity in Litres 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Tank Capacity:
• (a) Volume: 2 m × 1.5 m × 1 m = 3 cubic metres (3 m³).
• (b) Capacity in litres: 3 m³ × 1,000 litres/m³ = 3,000 litres.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Volume: 3 m³ 1.5 M
Capacity: 3,000 litres 1.5 M
Q10 A student's school bag has: 4 textbooks weighing 350 g each, 5 notebooks weighing 150 g each, a water bottle weighing 800 g, and a pencil box weighing 250 g. What is the total weight of the bag in kg and g? Textbook Exercise • Heavy School Bag Weight 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Total Weight Calculation:
• Textbooks: 4 × 350 g = 1,400 g.
• Notebooks: 5 × 150 g = 750 g.
• Water bottle: 800 g.
• Pencil box: 250 g.
• Sum in grams: 1,400 + 750 + 800 + 250 = 3,200 grams.
• In kg and g = 3 kg and 200 grams (3.2 kg).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Itemized weights calculated 1.5 M
Total: 3 kg 200 g 1.5 M
Q11 A solid metal cube of side 4 cm is dropped into a full container of water. How many millilitres of water will overflow? Textbook Exercise • Comparing Volumes of Liquid & Solid 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Water Displacement Principle:
• A submerged solid displaces an amount of water equal to its own volume.
• Volume of metal cube = 4 cm × 4 cm × 4 cm = 64 cm³.
• Since 1 cm³ = 1 mL, the volume of water displaced = 64 mL.
Therefore, 64 mL of water will overflow.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Volume of cube = 64 cm³ 1 M
Overflow = 64 mL 1 M
Q12 Find the volume of a cardboard box that is 45 cm long, 25 cm wide, and 20 cm high. Textbook Exercise • Cardboard Box Volume 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Volume Calculation:
• Volume = Length × Width × Height = 45 × 25 × 20 cm³.
• 25 × 20 = 500.
• 45 × 500 = 22,500 cm³.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Formula l × w × h 1 M
Answer: 22,500 cm³ 1 M
Q13 100 grains of rice weigh about 2 grams. (a) What is the weight of 1 grain of rice? (b) Approximately how many grains of rice are there in a 1 kg (1,000 g) bag? Textbook Exercise • Rice Grain Count Estimation 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Estimation:
• (a) Weight of 1 grain: 2 g ÷ 100 = 0.02 grams.
• (b) Grains in 1 kg: 1,000 g ÷ 2 g = 500 packets of 100 grains.
Total grains = 500 × 100 = 50,000 grains.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
1 grain: 0.02 g 1 M
1 kg has 50,000 grains 2 M
Q14 A rectangular wooden block is 12 cm × 9 cm × 6 cm. It is cut into small cubes of side 3 cm. How many small cubes can be cut without any wood wasted? Textbook Exercise • Cubes from a Large Wooden Block 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Cube Division:
• Along length: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 cubes.
• Along width: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 cubes.
• Along height: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 cubes.
• Total cubes: 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cubes.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Dimensions division (4 × 3 × 2) 1 M
Total: 24 cubes 1 M
Q15 A juice pack is a rectangular cuboid measuring 10 cm × 6 cm × 15 cm. (a) What is its volume in cm³? (b) How many litres of juice does it contain (assuming full)? Textbook Exercise • Juice Carton Content 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Volume & Capacity:
• (a) Volume: 10 × 6 × 15 = 900 cm³.
• (b) Capacity in litres: 900 cm³ = 900 mL = 900 ÷ 1,000 = 0.9 litres.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Volume: 900 cm³ 1 M
Capacity: 0.9 litres 1 M
Q16 A cube has side 2 cm. If its side is doubled to 4 cm: (a) Find original volume. (b) Find new volume. (c) By how many times does the volume increase? Textbook Exercise • Doubling Cube Side (Volume Effect) 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Volume Scaling:
• (a) Original: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 cm³.
• (b) New: 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cm³.
• (c) Increase factor: 64 ÷ 8 = 8 times larger (since 2³ = 8).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Original: 8 cm³ 1 M
New: 64 cm³ 1 M
Increases by 8 times 1 M
Q17 An ice cube has side 3 cm. When melted, does water occupy more, less, or equal volume to ice? (Scientific note: Ice expands when frozen; 100 cm³ ice produces ~92 mL water). Textbook Exercise • Ice Cube Melting Volume 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Observation:
• Volume of ice cube = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 cm³.
• Water occupies slightly less volume than ice because water expands when freezing. When 27 cm³ of ice melts, it produces about 25 mL of liquid water.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Volume calculation: 27 cm³ 1 M
Water occupies less volume explained 1 M
Q18 A pit 4 metres long, 3 metres wide, and 2 metres deep is dug in a field. How many cubic metres of earth (soil) were dug out? Textbook Exercise • Soil Dug from a Pit 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Volume of Excavation:
• Volume of earth dug = Length × Width × Depth = 4 m × 3 m × 2 m = 24 cubic metres (24 m³).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Formula l × w × d 1 M
Answer: 24 m³ 1 M
Q19 Explain why 1 kg of cotton wool occupies a much larger volume (space) than 1 kg of iron, even though their weights are equal. Textbook Exercise • Difference between Weight and Volume 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Density & Volume:
• Both have the exact same weight (1 kg).
• However, iron is very dense with closely packed particles, so 1 kg fits in a small space.
• Cotton is fluffy, porous, and contains a lot of trapped air, meaning its particles are loosely spread, so 1 kg occupies a huge physical space (large volume).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Equal mass/weight stated 1 M
Density & particle spacing explained 1 M
Q20 A 1-rupee coin weighs 4.85 grams. What is the total weight of 100 such 1-rupee coins in grams? Textbook Exercise • Weight of 100 One-Rupee Coins 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Multiplication:
• Total weight = 100 × 4.85 g = 485 grams.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Multiplication 100 × 4.85 1 M
Answer: 485 grams 1 M
Q21 A small rectangular children's pool is 10 m long, 5 m wide, and 1.2 m deep. What is the total volume of water needed to fill it to the brim in litres? Textbook Exercise • Swimming Pool Capacity 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Volume and Litres:
• Volume = 10 × 5 × 1.2 = 60 cubic metres.
• In litres = 60 × 1,000 litres = 60,000 litres.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Volume: 60 m³ 1.5 M
Capacity: 60,000 litres 1.5 M
Q22 A standard construction brick measures 20 cm × 10 cm × 8 cm. Find the volume of a stack containing 500 such bricks in cubic metres. Textbook Exercise • Brick Stacking Volume 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Brick Stack Volume:
• Volume of 1 brick = 20 × 10 × 8 = 1,600 cm³.
• Volume of 500 bricks = 500 × 1,600 = 800,000 cm³.
• In cubic metres: 1 m³ = 1,000,000 cm³.
• Volume = 800,000 ÷ 1,000,000 = 0.8 m³.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
1 brick: 1,600 cm³ 1 M
500 bricks: 800,000 cm³ 1 M
Converted to 0.8 m³ 1 M
Q23 On a two-pan balance scale, a watermelon on the left pan balances with: one 2 kg weight, one 500 g weight, and two 200 g weights on the right pan. What is the weight of the watermelon? Textbook Exercise • Balance Scale Weighing 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Weight Balance:
• 2 kg = 2,000 g.
• Weights on right pan = 2,000 + 500 + 200 + 200 = 2,900 grams (or 2 kg 900 g).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Sum of weights on pan 1 M
Watermelon weight: 2 kg 900 g 1 M
Q24 When reading the liquid level in a measuring cylinder, why should your eye be level with the bottom of the curved water surface (meniscus)? Textbook Exercise • Measuring Cylinder Meniscus 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Accurate Measurement:
• Due to surface tension, water curves upwards slightly at the container edges, forming a concave curved surface called a meniscus.
• Looking from above or below introduces parallax error. Keeping your eye directly level with the lowest point of the meniscus ensures an accurate and true volume reading.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Meniscus curvature explained 1 M
Avoiding parallax error explained 1 M
